title: The Fourth Crusade
objective: After this level you can explain how crusaders ended up sacking Christian Constantinople.
summary: In debt to Venice, the Fourth Crusade took Christian Zara, then followed an exiled prince to Constantinople, sacked it in April 1204 and ruled it as a Latin empire until 1261.

cards.headline: In 1204 crusaders sacked a Christian city: Constantinople.
cards.body: Nobody set out to do that. A debt, a deal and an exiled prince took them there.

cards.headline: A bill in Venice
cards.body: Pope Innocent III called a new crusade in 1198. The crusaders hired Venice to ship them east for 85,000 marks. But when the army gathered in 1202, only about a third of the expected men turned up, and they couldn’t pay. To settle the debt, in November 1202 they attacked and took Zara (Zadar), a Christian city. Imagine booking a bus for thirty friends when only ten show up. The driver still wants the full fare.

cards.headline: A prince’s offer
cards.body: Then came a tempting offer. An exiled Byzantine prince, Alexius, promised the crusaders a huge payment, the Byzantine church’s submission to Rome and help on crusade, if they would put him on the throne in Constantinople. The fleet turned toward the city.

cards.headline: Over the walls from the water
cards.body: Remember Level 4’s walls, which held against attackers through the early Middle Ages? In 1204 the attack came from the water. On 12 April, men climbed from ships’ masts across catwalks onto the walls. For three days the army pillaged at will, defiling and stealing from the holy places. Justinian’s Hagia Sophia, from Level 5, was looted. The four bronze horses of St Mark’s in Venice were brought from Constantinople at this time.

cards.headline: A Latin empire
cards.body: The crusaders made Baldwin of Flanders emperor of a new Latin empire, and Hagia Sophia became a Roman Catholic cathedral. When Pope Innocent III heard how the crusaders had behaved, he was filled with shame and rebuked them. In 1261 Michael VIII Palaeologus retook a much diminished Constantinople. The Crusades had begun with a call to aid the Christians of the East. This one wrecked their capital.

mascot.line: This is Level 41’s call for help, turned upside down.

questions.prompt: Which city did the Fourth Crusade sack in April 1204?
questions.explanation: On 12 April 1204 the crusaders broke into Constantinople and pillaged it for three days.

questions.prompt: Why did the Fourth Crusade attack Zara, a Christian city, in 1202?

options.label: To settle the crusaders’ debt to Venice
Zara was the capital of Byzantium
Its ruler had broken an oath to Alexius

questions.explanation: Only about a third of the army arrived and it could not pay Venice’s 85,000 marks, so the crusaders took Zara to settle the debt.

questions.prompt: Level 4’s walls held Constantinople through the early Middle Ages. How did the crusaders get in on 12 April 1204?

options.label: They tunnelled under the land walls
options.rationale: The attack came from the water.

options.label: Byzantine soldiers opened the gates for them
They climbed onto the walls from ships

questions.explanation: In 1204 the attack came from the water: men climbed from ships’ masts across catwalks onto the walls.
